title: State of Play Highlights PS5 and Asian Game News
seoTitle: State of Play Highlights PS5 and Asian Game News
subtitle: Sony Broadcast Two Special Editions of the Event This Thursday, September 3rd
excerpt: Sony presented two State of Play editions on September 3, featuring new trailers, gameplay from Western titles, and a special focus on games.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Sony broadcast two editions of State of Play this Thursday, September 3rd, sparking great interest among PlayStation fans. The first block brought news on games from PlayStation Studios and Western partners; the second, hosted by Yuki Kaji, focused on Japanese and other Asian productions.

What Was Presented in the First State of Play Edition

In the first broadcast, the Japanese giant showcased unreleased trailers and gameplay from titles by major studios and independent developers. Among the highlights, the new Resident Evil film received exclusive scenes, with director Zach Cregger appearing at the end to confirm that the movie hits theaters on September 18th.

Final Fantasy VII Revelation Takes Center Stage at State of Play Japan

The second edition, named State of Play Japan, dedicated part of its broadcast to the RPG Final Fantasy VII Revelation, the third and final part of Square Enix's remake trilogy. The event provided in-depth information on Vincent Valentine's gameplay and combat, complementing what was revealed at Gamescom 2026.

Broadcast Dates and Platforms

Both presentations were live at 10 AM (Brasília time) and could be watched on PlayStation's official YouTube and Twitch channels. Sony did not disclose the exact duration of each block.

Upcoming Releases Announced

In addition to the Resident Evil film and Final Fantasy VII Revelation, State of Play included other titles not yet officially listed. The event reinforced the PS5's release schedule, indicating that the platform's ecosystem will continue to receive new content throughout the next year.

Expectations for the Future of PS5

Even with the end of physical media, Sony signaled that the console's future remains promising, by investing in exclusive content and partnerships with studios from different regions. The September 3rd State of Play demonstrates the company's strategy to keep the audience engaged with regular releases, focusing on both Western and Asian productions.

With information from TecMundo, Olhar Digital.
